_note: Baseline shell_execute verbs pre-approved for the Personal audience.
netclaw matches these as command prefixes, the same way the live
tool-approvals.json records them.
Caveat, observed on 0.25.3: the daemon prompted for 'git fetch origin
dev' even with 'git fetch' approved, so prefix matching is narrower
than the line above assumes. Longer verbs get seeded as they surface.
Source 1: the permissions.allow list from a Claude Code workspace
settings.json, translated from its syntax (Bash(x:*) -> x).
WebSearch, WebFetch(domain:...) and mcp__* entries are dropped:
netclaw governs those through AllowedTools and MCP grants, not
shell_execute.
Source 2: binaries newly available via /tools.
rtk-prefixed twins are included because rtk is now on PATH and is the
token-cheap path for read-heavy commands.
git commit is deliberately absent: it is in the source file's 'ask'
list, not 'allow'. git push is absent for the same reason except for
'git push fork', which supports the fork-and-PR workflow (gh repo fork,
git remote add fork, push, open a PR) without granting push to origin.
Caveat: 'git remote add fork' and 'git remote set-url origin' are also
seeded, so the 'fork' remote can be pointed at any URL before pushing --
the destination is not pinned to the operator's GitHub account.
Broader than the rest, inherited from the dev sandbox where a human
watches every call -- revisit if netclaw runs unattended on a schedule:
sops        decrypts secrets (whole binary); sops exec-env and
exec-file run a command with secrets in its environment
ssh         (as /tools/bin/ssh) remote exec + network egress;
-o ProxyCommand=<cmd> runs a local command, no connection
git config  alias.*, core.pager, credential.helper values execute on
the next git invocation
dotnet tool install pulls any NuGet tool, dotnet tool run executes it
curl        arbitrary network egress; -o can write files anywhere
sed/mv/mkdir/cp/chmod mutating; sed -i can rewrite any readable file,
chmod can flip anything executable
git checkout/merge/branch mutate worktree and refs; 'git checkout --
<path>' discards local edits, 'git branch -D' deletes
gh issue create posts publicly to any repo the token can reach
Never seeded (mutate infrastructure or data): kubectl apply/delete/edit,
helm install/upgrade, terraform apply/destroy, aws write APIs, psql,
tcpdump, rsync.
